rail_guard.text: Sheffield Station. Trains for every station you have visited in England, Wales and Scotland. Please take your steel, your relish and your football scarf with you.

shf_steelman.text: Thirty-eight years in the melting shop. It was hot enough to fry an egg on a bar, and we did, most Fridays.
The best steel, Crucible steel, was poured from white-hot pots, and the ring when you tapped it was like a church bell. That's the sound I miss.

then.text: You've had the full tour, love. You can have the rest of the year's stories, but I'd want paying in tea.

else.text: The old steelworker nods at the gates of the museum. Take the tour?

then.text: Right. Hard hat, love. Safety first, then egg.
The museum's great furnace is cold now, but the old man puts a hand on the brick and the whole shed seems to remember.
He shows you the crucible pots, the tongs as long as a lamp-post, the tiny marks on a bar where a worker signed his work with a chisel, so that nobody would forget who made it.
Cutlery, razors, bridges, ships. Sheffield made the knife and the fork that you eat your tea with. Sheffield steel's in the Eiffel Tower, if you squint, and I always do.
That's the tour. Here, take a pork pie. It's from the canteen. There are three left from 1987. Not those. These are this week's.

else.text: Another day, then. The furnace will keep. It's the one thing in this city that has always kept its temper.

then.text: Rainy day? Perfect. Snooker's an indoor sport, love. It's basically made for Sheffield.
Evening session's about to start at the Crucible. Quiet as a mouse in there.

shf_snooker.text: The Crucible seats 980, and it's the quietest 980 you'll ever hear. You could hear a chalk drop.
Cue ball, red, colour, red, colour. It's maths with a stick, and a lot of nerves. I could watch it for hours. I have.

then.text: Rain again. I'm playing it with feeling. The feeling is 'damp'.
Sun's out! Folk are tipping in coins and chips. I'll take both.

shf_busker.text: Some lads from just up the road made an album in a bedroom and now people write songs about the city's chip shops. I do the same. No one writes about me.
I've been told to 'play it with feeling'. I'm told the feeling is mostly cold.

shf_relish.text: Henderson's Relish: Sheffield's secret sauce, a thin dark liquid that goes with everything. The recipe is known only to a few people. They've taken a vow, and I've seen them. They look very calm.
We have a saying: if you leave Sheffield, it follows you. Usually in a bottle in your luggage.

then.text: Jogging in the rain, me. Builds character. Also ruins your hat, if you've got one.
Windy up the hills today! I'm jogging into it and going backwards.

shf_fullmonty.text: A famous film about six lads who lost their jobs at the steelworks was set right here, and I should say it was funny and kind in equal parts.
People still stop me and ask where they can get the hat. I tell them it was a small hat. They understand.

then.text: Rain on all seven hills. Uphill in the wet builds character, apparently. I've loads of character.
Fog in Sheffield! Can't see the hill, but my legs know it's there, love.
Up for a nine o'clock lecture. That's dawn for a student. Don't laugh.

shf_student.text: {greeting} Two universities, sixty thousand students, and a hill on every route. The first week, everyone says 'I'll take the bus'. By week three they say 'where's the gym?'
The city got a tram in 1994. It goes up the hill. It doesn't go down. Or it goes down very quietly.

sheffield_steelworker.text: Night shift at the works. Sheffield's still making steel, love, just a bit quieter than it used to.
My grandad worked nights on the Don. He said the furnaces lit the whole valley orange.
Stars are out over the hills. Shame I'll be indoors for them. Still, it's a good job.

sheffield_night_nurse.text: Off up to the Northern General for the night. Uphill, of course. It's Sheffield.
Lovely and quiet at this hour. Just me, the trams and a fox on the corner.
Get to bed, love. If you need me later, I'll be the one with the tea.

sheffield_bowler.text: I cut it twice a week and people still say it's slow. It is not slow. They are just not very good.
